rationale: Starting from scratch, I designed a balanced robot geometry with 5 sensors spread evenly across the front to detect the tape line effectively. I chose a moderate sensor size (0.012 m) to balance resolution and coverage. The wheel track and body width are set to 0.12 m to allow stable turning without excessive width that would increase off-track risk. The wheel radius is 0.035 m for a good compromise between speed and torque, and mass is set to 0.8 kg for moderate inertia. The controller uses a base speed of 1.2 to aim for a good pace without risking instability. PID gains are set to moderate values (kp=8, ki=0.5, kd=3) to provide responsive but stable steering. Sensor weights are arranged to steer left when the line is detected on the right sensors and vice versa, with stronger weights on the outer sensors to enhance correction. The line loss strategy is 'search_left' to attempt recovery by turning right when the line is lost. I request a broad set of observations including completion, progress, errors, line loss events, and control effort to analyze performance and guide future improvements.
